sourceRef.title: Interacting with Docker Containers - Shell and SSH

sentences.text: When you SSH into a container, you're essentially treating it like a traditional virtual machine, which goes against the container philosophy of **isolated**, **ephemeral**, and minimalistic environments.

sourceRef.title: Interacting with Docker Containers - Shell and SSH

sentences.text: **Security Risks**: SSH servers add unnecessary complexity and potential vulnerabilities to your container.

sourceRef.title: Interacting with Docker Containers - Shell and SSH

sentences.text: Each SSH process running in a container is an additional attack surface for malicious actors.

sourceRef.title: Interacting with Docker Containers - Shell and SSH

sentences.text: **Container Bloat**: Containers are meant to be lightweight and contain only the essential packages needed to run the application.

sourceRef.title: Interacting with Docker Containers - Shell and SSH

sentences.text: Installing an SSH server and shell increases the size of the container and adds extra layers that are not necessary for the application to function.

sourceRef.title: Interacting with Docker Containers - Shell and SSH

sentences.text: **Deviation from Container Orchestration Tools**: Modern container orchestration tools like Kubernetes provide their own methods for accessing containers, such as kubectl exec .

sourceRef.title: Interacting with Docker Containers - Shell and SSH

sentences.text: Using SSH and shell can bypass these tools, leading to a deviation from standardized workflows and potentially causing configuration drift.

sourceRef.title: Interacting with Docker Containers - Shell and SSH

sentences.text: **Statefulness**: Containers are designed to be stateless and immutable.

sourceRef.title: Interacting with Docker Containers - Shell and SSH

sentences.text: SSH'ing and shell into a container and making changes can lead to a stateful configuration that is not reflected in the container's image or definition files.

sourceRef.title: Interacting with Docker Containers - Shell and SSH

sentences.text: This can cause issues when the container is redeployed or scaled across different environments.

sourceRef.title: Interacting with Docker Containers - Shell and SSH

sentences.text: **Lifecycle Management**: Docker containers are meant to be stopped and started frequently, with changes being made through updates to the container image.

sourceRef.title: Interacting with Docker Containers - Shell and SSH

sentences.text: By using SSH and shell, you might be tempted to make ad-hoc changes to the running container, which is against the principles of immutable infrastructure.

sourceRef.title: Interacting with Docker Containers - Shell and SSH

sentences.text: **Complexity in Management**: Managing SSH keys, ensuring they are rotated and kept secure, adds an additional layer of complexity to container management.

sourceRef.title: Interacting with Docker Containers - Shell and SSH

sentences.text: It also increases the administrative overhead of managing access to containers.

sourceRef.title: Interacting with Docker Containers - Shell and SSH

sentences.text: Whether you prefer the simplicity of Docker exec or the persistence of SSH, both methods provide robust ways to interact with your Docker containers.

sourceRef.title: Interacting with Docker Containers - Shell and SSH

sentences.text: Remember to use these tools responsibly, keeping security in mind, and you'll be able to manage your containers effectively.
